quest.title: Tales From the Court
quest.description: Staelle seems to be in a spot of trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Please, help me out! I was just thinking about the novel's story, and before I knew it, Barea was just gone!

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Are you sure you didn't leave it at your seat in the opera house, or left it tied to the restroom door, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: I've already searched all those areas. I've even looked under that seat, but Barea wasn't there.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Oh, the mere thought of it, that my little Barea would be kidnapped by someone, or perhaps follow someone blindly as if stricken by puppy love...

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Ms. Staelle, I'm quite sure that Barea wouldn't make the same mistake twice like that.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Ah, but my Barry-boo is still so little... and little children make the same errors many times, and even revel in it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: I'm... quite certain that Barea is not as young as you say.

choices.text: And who's this Barea, if I might ask?

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Yep. Her family has gone missing, and she's asking for my help.

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Ms. Staelle, we have already searched this area once. I would wager that Barea has headed off into the wilds.

response.speaker: Staelle
response.text: Then let us go there too!

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Please, Miss, I ask you to stay in the city. With the dress you wear, you would not be able to catch Barea even if you found it.

response.speaker: Staelle
response.text: Nonsense! Why, Barea would jump into my arms if it so much as saw me!

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Then I suppose it heard us not when we were calling up and down the theater, yes?

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Well, there you have it. I'm afraid I cannot bring Barea back to Ms. Staelle alone.

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: I cannot simply leave my post for long, much less ask another colleague to leave theirs with me.

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: But if you're willing, Traveler, could you help us both out?

choices.text: Well, it wouldn't be a problem, per se...

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Well, that's settled, then. Please come with me to the wilds — we shall look for Barea together.

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Considering its weight and stamina, it cannot have run too far.

response.speaker: Staelle
response.text: What!? My Barea is most healthy, thank you!

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: I would agree — if we were talking about its mental health.

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: Let us be off — lest Barea gain a taste for the outdoors and run still further away.

choices.text: You police need to deal with this stuff too?

response.speaker: Blathine
response.text: If the citizens of the Court of Fontaine ask me for help, I have no reason to refuse them.

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Well, there it is — and looking quite good, too.

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: I wonder when Ms. Staelle will realize that dogs have no love for the opera, or for her novels?

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Let us return — she's probably worried sick.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Barea! Oh, my baby! Where have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: It simply found a quiet spot to rest for a while. A bit of a vacation, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Ah, I was so worried! Thank you, Officer Blathine, thank you! You will be in my next novel for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Thank you for your consideration, but it might be best if you save the ink — I doubt anyone would be all that interested in the daily life of a police officer.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Then I'll simply have to dramatize your tale... It will be interesting, I swear!

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: That promise of yours is already too much drama for me, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Ah, the conclusion's got to be inspiring! Let me think — who shall I assign to be your partner...

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Is it that Barea doesn't like my new novel? *sigh* But everyone else thinks it's pretty good...

dialogues.speaker: Staelle
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should read it a nicer passage...

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Barea dislikes places that are too lively. The opera house probably disturbed it and inspired its escape.

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: It might be hiding in the bushes... Let's head to the patch over there.

dialogues.speaker: Blathine
dialogues.text: Not here... Hmmm, let's head elsewhere...
